diagnostic_evidence.quote: is a quadratic matrix polynomial, having $q$ eigenvalues at 0, $q$ eigenvalues at infinity

issues.failure_explanation: The stated hypotheses do not imply that the displayed rational function is a quadratic polynomial. For example, in a one-dimensional block take S1=2, S2=1, U1=V2=X=Y=1 and A(z)=1-3z+2z^2. Both displayed hypotheses hold, but the defined product is -2z(1-2z)/(2-z), whereas the stated coefficient formulas give the polynomial -z. The later application also does not satisfy the stated condition: substituting S1^{-1}=Lambda_{R,1} produces inverse powers of Lambda_{R,1} and a term Lambda_{G,1}A2, whereas equation (10) supplies the different left-solvent relation quoted above.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the displayed left-shift hypothesis by a valid left-invariant condition, add any missing compatibility hypotheses, and reprove the coefficient and factorization conclusions before applying them in Section 3.
issues.overall_effect: The block-shifted polynomial, its stated coefficients and eigenvalue relocation, the subsequent factorization and block reduction, and the theoretical foundation of the BS-CR algorithms are unsupported.
issues.title: The block-shift theorem has a false left-invariance condition
issues.why_classification: A contained correction and reproof of the cited block-shift theorem can preserve the subsequent architecture and intended scope, but it is a nontrivial mathematical replacement rather than a typographical edit.

issues.failure_explanation: The assumptions expressly allow an eigenvalue at infinity, which puts the eigenvalue 0 into Lambda_{R,1}. Then no finite nonsingular S1 satisfies S1^{-1}=Lambda_{R,1}, so the rational deflation and Theorem th5 cannot be invoked. This is not an excluded degenerate case: Example 1 has lambda_8=infinity. Consequently, the premise that the reduced matrix G-bar satisfies the reduced QME is not established in this regime.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply a direct algebraic or limiting treatment of singular Lambda_{R,1}; otherwise impose det Lambda_{R,1} != 0 and explicitly exclude infinite-root cases, including the present Example 1.
issues.overall_effect: The reduced block systems, the B-coefficients, and the theoretical justification of Algorithm alg:gfull are unreliable precisely for allowed and tested problems having roots at infinity.
issues.title: The deflation is undefined when Lambda_R,1 has a zero eigenvalue
issues.why_classification: A contained singular-case lemma or a limited restriction to finite roots can preserve a comparable method, but the current proof cannot be repaired by notation alone.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: as $k \rightarrow \infty$,  $a_k(z)$ has exactly $m-\ell$ zeros that converge to 0, which implies that

issues.failure_explanation: Eigenvalues tending to zero do not make A_0^{(k)} exactly rank-deficient at any finite k. Nullity is integer-valued; a sequence of nonsingular matrices can converge to a matrix of nullity m-ell while every term has nullity 0. In Example 3 all inside eigenvalues are positive, so the quoted root property gives det A_0^{(k)} != 0 rather than nullity m-ell. The subsequent inference that the last m-ell right or left singular vectors converge to the invariant subspaces requires an additional singular-value gap and subspace perturbation argument, which is not supplied.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must prove a persistent singular-value gap and convergence of the corresponding singular subspaces, with finite-k error and termination estimates, under explicit hypotheses.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed extraction of W_{G,1}, Lambda_{G,1}, T_{R,1}, and Lambda_{R,1}, the termination criterion and exact output guarantee of Algorithm alg:isg, and consequently Algorithm alg:gfull are unsupported.
issues.title: Small limiting eigenvalues do not imply the stated nullities or SVD-subspace convergence
issues.why_classification: The missing argument is the central convergence justification for the proposed subspace extraction and algorithm; the source provides no complete replacement proof.

issues.failure_explanation: In the SVD A2=U Sigma V^T, the left singular vectors are the columns of U. A row basis for the small left singular subspace is therefore formed from the last rows of U^T, equivalently the transposes of the last columns of U. Partitioning and returning U itself generally produces rows unrelated to that left singular subspace, so T_R need not approximate or satisfy T_{R,1}R=Lambda_{R,1}T_{R,1}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Partition (U_2^{(k)})^T into row blocks, or equivalently take T_R=(U_2^{(k)})^T, and use its last m-ell rows consistently in the Lambda_{R,1} formula.
issues.overall_effect: As written, Algorithm alg:isg can return the wrong left invariant subspace, making the shifted coefficients and the final R computed by Algorithm alg:gfull incorrect.
issues.title: The left singular subspace uses rows of U rather than rows of U transpose
issues.why_classification: The correction is a local transpose convention change; the convergence strategy, outputs, and computational architecture are otherwise unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The algorithm performs every CR step and computes the displayed recovery matrices unconditionally. Its input contract does not assume that all A_1^{(k)} are nonsingular or that the accepted hat-A_1 matrix is nonsingular, and the preceding convergence proposition assumes only CR boundedness and absence of breakdown, not invertibility of hat-A_1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add explicit no-breakdown and hat-A_1 nonsingularity hypotheses, together with algorithmic singularity checks and a defined failure or fallback path.
issues.overall_effect: For otherwise admissible inputs, Algorithm alg:isg can break down or attempt an undefined inverse, so its stated output guarantee is conditional on omissions that are not checked.
issues.title: Required CR and recovery-matrix inverses are not guaranteed or checked
issues.why_classification: The missing conditions may exclude an uncharacterized part of the advertised input class; adding them is more than a purely local typo correction, although no global redesign is required.

issues.failure_explanation: An arbitrary generalized Schur decomposition does not put one copy of each mu_i in the leading ell-by-ell block. Because every eigenvalue has multiplicity two, the leading block may contain two copies of one mu_i and none of another, yielding the wrong solvent or a leading subspace that is not the graph needed for Z11 and Q11 to be invertible.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use an ordered/selective QZ decomposition that places one eigenvalue from each double pair mu_i in the leading block, and verify the associated graph-space invertibility conditions.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm alg:QZ does not guarantee the unique solution G-bar_11 with spectrum mu_1,...,mu_ell, and therefore Algorithm alg:gfull can reconstruct the wrong G and R.
issues.title: The QZ step does not select the required deflating subspace
issues.why_classification: Standard QZ reordering supplies the missing selection without changing the method, its complexity model, or its intended guarantee.

If the test fails, G-bar_21 and R-bar_12 are not computed, yet the algorithm still proceeds to the final reconstruction formulas. diagnostic_evidence.quote: $a(z)$ has $\ell$ distinct roots $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_\ell$ of modulus $1$, each with multiplicity 2

issues.failure_explanation: In Case 3 the values 1 and -1 each occur twice. Under the displayed construction, det(zI-G) and det(zR-I) each contribute another copy of every repeated mu, so those repeated values have algebraic multiplicity four, not two. The experiment therefore also violates the standing requirement that the ell unit roots be distinct; the text only acknowledges a departure through complex entries, not repeated roots.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose eight distinct unit-modulus values and rerun the case, or remove/relabel Case 3; retaining the repeated values would require extending the theory and algorithmic justification to repeated unit eigenvalues.
issues.overall_effect: The ell=8 experiment does not test the stated theory or support the claimed multiplicity-two setting, weakening the reported robustness evidence for that case.
issues.title: Example 3 uses repeated unit eigenvalues despite claiming multiplicity two
issues.why_classification: Repair requires replacement numerical evidence or a nontrivial extension to repeated roots; simply editing the surrounding sentence would leave the test outside the paper's assumptions.
